newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast Lt. crudes jump with NYMEX Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast Lt. crudes jump with NYMEX Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot crude markets remained idle Monday, with refiners on the sidelines as crude reversed Friday's sharp gains by falling 53 cents a gallon, traders said.

In futures markets, June deliveries of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude dropped 53 cents a barrel to $21.59, leaving buyers nervous about the volatile market for raw materials with refined product margins still low.
The benchmark West Coast grade, Alaska North Slope (ANS), tracked the fall in futures and spot markets.
Outright ANS prices fell 60 cents a barrel to $19.90/20.10 a barrel.
Meanwhile, ANS discounts have remained stagnant since a cargo sold in early May at $1.50 a barrel under WTI.
BP continued to offer ANS at $1.30 under WTI as it waited for the July contract, which ended 31 cents higher, to become the nearby contract on Wednesday.
Kern River crude prices rose after more California oil companies reported increased postings Monday. The heavy grade average price stood $15.32/15.42 a barrel.
Line 63 markets remained idle, while asphalt crude Wilmington rose with postings to $17.17/17.27.
